editorial: This report contains trends that have emerged for the first time today, without repeating records included in normal reports from the last 30 days.

items.title: cursor/plugins
items.summary: Cursor, an AI-powered code editor, has released an official plugin specification for developers to create their own extensions. This standard allows for extending the editor's capabilities and creating customizable workflows through TypeScript-based plugins.

items.title: tile-ai/tilelang
items.summary: Tilelang is a domain-specific language that facilitates the development of high-performance graphics processing unit (GPU), central processing unit (CPU), and accelerator kernels. This Python-based tool simplifies complex hardware optimization processes, allowing software developers to create more efficient computing units.

items.title: pablostanley/yoinks
items.summary: Yoinks is a tool for downloading any video via the terminal without ads or redirects. Developed with TypeScript, this software offers a practical method for transferring video files directly to local storage.

items.title: HunxByts/GhostTrack
items.summary: Developed with Python, GhostTrack is a tool that allows for location tracking via phone numbers. It provides users with a technical capability to detect the geographical information of target numbers.

items.title: Friedrich-M/UniMate
items.summary: UniMate is an animation technology used to animate different skeletal structures through a single model. Presented at SIGGRAPH Asia 2026, this work aims to standardize character animation processes.

items.title: Pi 1.0
items.summary: Pi 1.0 is a workflow orchestration tool that integrates with Pi Durable, a high-performance computing library. It facilitates fault-tolerant task execution in distributed systems by breaking complex processes into manageable parts.

items.title: StreetComplete on iOS is now in public beta
items.summary: The open-source map editing tool StreetComplete has launched a public beta for its iOS version, which allows users to easily update geographical data. The application provides a simple survey interface to verify local information and complete missing data on OpenStreetMap.

items.title: Clef: Open-weight decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
items.summary: Cloudflare has launched the Clef platform, which enables fine-tuning with open-weight decision models and reinforcement learning. This infrastructure supports developers in training AI models with their own private data to make more accurate decisions.

items.title: Pi Durable
items.summary: Pi Durable offers optimization methods at both hardware and software levels for the long-term and reliable operation of single-board computers like the Raspberry Pi. It suggests power management and data storage strategies to increase the durability of systems against environmental factors.

items.title: Git 3.0's upcoming SHA-256 default will be a costly mistake
items.summary: The Git version control system plans to transition its default hashing algorithm from SHA-1 to SHA-256 in future updates. Software developers argue that this change will create compatibility issues with existing projects and that the transition process will be costly.

items.title: Cloudflare/clef
items.summary: Clef, an image-to-text model developed by Cloudflare, analyzes visual data to generate text-based outputs. Thanks to its multimodal structure, the model is used in processes of interpreting and processing complex visual content.

items.title: LOCI: Spatial Linear Memory for Streaming World Models
items.summary: LOCI is a spatial linear memory architecture used to preserve past visual data in video world models. This structure solves the problem of remembering past observations and matching them with the current perspective in long-term video streams using a hybrid approach.

items.title: PhysVista: Benchmarking Physical Intelligence in VLMs via a Perception-Reasoning-Assessment Loop
items.summary: PhysVista is an evaluation framework that measures the ability of vision-language models to understand the movement and consistency rules of objects in the physical world. It tests whether models can make realistic inferences about real-world dynamics by addressing perception, reasoning, and physical judgment processes in an integrated loop.

items.title: Latent-Foresight: End-to-End Learning Predictable Representations for Latent World Models
items.summary: Latent-Foresight offers an end-to-end learning method that predicts future scene changes in the feature space of Vision Foundation Models. This approach eliminates the complexity of existing two-stage systems by combining data compression and prediction processes into a single model.

items.title: Generalization Is Stability, Not Accuracy: Multi-Axis Evaluation of LLMs
items.summary: Generalization ability in large language models (LLM) is defined by the capacity to produce consistent and semantically stable outputs even when the same input is expressed in different forms. Unlike existing studies, this approach evaluates model success on an individual sample basis across different input variations rather than a single accuracy score.

items.title: Removing the NEEDLE in the Haystack: Backdoor Removal in LLMs via Weight Orthogonalisation
items.summary: NEEDLE is a training-free method that aims to remove harmful backdoor triggers embedded in large language models during training without degrading the model's overall performance. This technique uses weight orthogonalization to clean only the targeted harmful behaviors without changing the model's output distribution.

items.title: Reducing the cognitive load of AI changes
items.summary: The integration of artificial intelligence tools into software development processes increases the frequency of context switching for developers, thereby raising cognitive load. This situation reveals that workflows must be designed to be less distracting to prevent loss of focus in AI-assisted coding processes.

glossary.explanation: A special text editor used by developers while writing code, which makes it easier to see and edit errors.
A set of technical rules and standards that must be followed to develop an extension for software.
A special processor that accelerates intensive mathematical operations such as image processing and artificial intelligence calculations.
The main processor that handles all basic commands on the computer and is considered the brain of the system.
The most basic core part of the operating system that manages the communication between the computer's hardware and software.
A special-purpose programming language designed to solve problems in a specific domain.
